subject: Question : what is the appropriate way to extend checkboxGroupInput to support titatoggle.css

messages.author: ce4116ba0e74c394
messages.subject: Question : what is the appropriate way to extend checkboxGroupInput to support titatoggle.css
parts:
Hi,

I've had a little luck extending checkboxGroupInput for my own needs.

I'm pretty sure this is an inelegant way to approach extending checkboxGroupInput ... I will say that it does indeed work

from input-checkboxgroup.R

I have my own divClass as such:

#divClass <- "form-group shiny-input-checkboxgroup shiny-input-container"
divClass <-
"form-group checkbox checkbox-slider--b shiny-input-checkboxgroup shiny-input-container"

and I return a css with the div as such:

# return label and select tag
#tags$div(id = inputId,
#         style = if (!is.null(width)) paste0("width: ", shiny::validateCssUnit(width), ";"),
#         class = divClass,
#         controlLabel(inputId, label),
#         options
#)
tagList(
  shiny::singleton(shiny::tags$head(
    shiny::tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css", href = "titatoggle-dist.css")
  )),
  div(
    id = inputId,
    style = if (!is.null(width))
      paste0("width: ", shiny::validateCssUnit(width), ";"),
    class = divClass,
    controlLabel(inputId, label),
    options
  )
)

I then include the titatoggle-dist.css in my www folder and it seems to work just fine. I just think there must be a better way than modifying the existing shiny source code or cut/copying/pasting non exported functions? Or is this how one would go about extending an existing input source?

I saw some examples here but https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/building-inputs.html not seeing or understanding the connection

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Question : what is the appropriate way to extend checkboxGroupInput to support titatoggle.css
parts: If you're just changing the cosmetics, I think that's a fine way. We make no guarantee that the underlying JS code you're relying on won't change, but in most cases I think you're still better off doing what you're doing then writing a completely new JS binding that's just the same as the existing one.
